question:
A 25-year-old woman presents with right-sided lower back pain that began a few days ago. She is
uncertain of the exact onset but believes it started after waking up one morning. The pain is localized to
the lower back and does not radiate. She has a history of two pregnancies (G2P2) and delivered her
second child via normal spontaneous vaginal delivery one year ago. She denies any additional
symptoms. On examination, the right sacral sulcus is shallow, and the right inferior lateral angle is
superior. There is tenderness in the lower lumbar paraspinal muscles bilaterally, and the seated flexion
test is positive on the left. What is the most likely diagnosis? Answer Choices: (A) Bilateral sacral
flexion about the middle transverse axis (B) Left-on-left sacral torsion (C) Right unilateral sacral flexion
about the middle transverse axis (D) Left unilateral sacral flexion about the superior transverse axis (E)
Right unilateral sacral extension about the superior transverse axis (F) Left sacral rotation on a right
oblique axis (G) Right unilateral sacral flexion about the superior transverse axis (H) Left unilateral
sacral extension about the middle transverse axis (I) Right-on-left sacral torsion (J) Left unilateral
sacral flexion about the middle transverse axis
 A. Left sacral rotation on a right oblique axis
B. Bilateral sacral flexion about the middle transverse axis
C. Left unilateral sacral flexion about the middle transverse axis
D. Left unilateral sacral extension about the middle transverse axis
E. Right unilateral sacral flexion about the superior transverse axis
F. Right unilateral sacral extension about the superior transverse axis
G. Left-on-left sacral torsion
H. Right-on-left sacral torsion
I. Right unilateral sacral flexion about the middle transverse axis
J. Left unilateral sacral flexion about the superior transverse axis
